summary: Discussion signals: govt ban on DeepSeek, NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, banks blocking third‑party agents, rising low‑cost agent sandboxes, OpenHands release, LayerFS and other infra/user workflow posts; several repo-only tools need corroboration. | Vendor-shard screening: prioritize three high-confidence infra/security advisories (GHSA), two OpenAI platform releases, AWS vendor case studies and operator/how-to posts, plus a mix of MCP/sandbox infra guidance and vendor product updates. | GitHub OSS snapshot: several vendor releases (Cloudflare, Microsoft, Vercel) and high‑traction agent platforms (Sim, ruflo) plus emerging infra primitives (Agent2API gateway, xerj MCP/search, Hotcell sandboxes). No social/user-field reports in this shard; several small repos need corroboration. | Package-land signals show expanding agent sandbox, eval, memory, and VS Code agent ecosystems: Amazon and OpenAI packages stand out; multiple infra primitives (agent sandboxes, eval frameworks, detection, memory) merit follow-up and social corroboration.

candidates.title: DeepSeek banned from U.S. federal civilian agencies
candidates.why_it_matters: Federal ban constrains vendor adoption and procurement risk for agent tooling.
candidates.next_check: Watch for vendor statement or US/DHS guidance; check vendor customer churn metrics.

candidates.title: NVIDIA OpenShell open‑source safe runtime for agent fleets
candidates.why_it_matters: Runtime enforces kernel‑level sandboxes and prevents agents holding credentials.
candidates.next_check: Track adoption reports, security audits, and any vendor integrations (NVIDIA GTC materials).

candidates.title: US banks blocking third‑party AI agents from customer accounts
candidates.why_it_matters: Real operational impact: banks and integrators losing agent access to accounts.
candidates.next_check: Monitor bank notices, PSD2/Open Banking guidance, and third‑party vendor mitigation patterns.

candidates.title: New low‑cost agent sandboxes: Runtime (runtm) and Agent37
